candidate_sentences.text: Passenger volumes declined modestly by 0.9% to 5.5 million, but cargo units fell significantly by 19.2% to 245,004 and passenger vehicles decreased by 2.2% to 760,473.

verified_key_information_units.information: Key performance drivers included weak consumer and business confidence, geopolitical tensions impacting demand; fleet optimization through vessel sales and continued chartering; cost efficiency measures; and a depreciation expense decline from aligning cruise/passenger vessel useful lives to 45 years (excluding shuttle vessels).
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Management Report: 'The following operational factors impacted...' section and 'Earnings' section detailing depreciation impact and strategic focus on cost efficiencies.

candidate_sentences.text: AS Tallink Grupp’s financial performance weakened in 2025 amid subdued consumer and business confidence, economic challenges in its core markets and heightened geopolitical tensions.

Lower depreciation, resulting mainly from extending the estimated useful lives of most cruise and passenger vessels to 45 years, reduced costs by EUR 18.0 million and partly offset weaker operating performance.
Overall, 2025 reflected lower demand and weaker profitability, alongside active fleet rationalisation, debt reduction and continued cost-efficiency measures.

verified_key_information_units.information: Fleet management involved the sale of three vessels (passenger vessel Star I in April, cargo vessels Regal Star in August and Sailor in October) and reduction of lay-up vessels from four to zero by Q3 2025; three vessels (Romantika, Galaxy I, Silja Europa) remained chartered out at year-end.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Management Report: Bullet points under operational factors listing vessel sales, lay-up reductions, and chartering details.

verified_key_information_units.information: Segment performance: Estonia-Finland route revenue increased EUR 1.7 million to EUR 314.5 million (passenger volumes up 1.8%) while Finland-Sweden routes declined EUR 3.3 million to EUR 225.5 million (due to maintenance) and Estonia-Sweden routes fell EUR 12.1 million to EUR 85.3 million (passenger volumes down 12.5%).
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Management Report: 'Sales and Segments' section breaking down revenue and results by route, including passenger/cargo unit changes and maintenance impacts.

candidate_sentences.text: Passenger numbers increased 1.8% on the Estonia–Finland route but declined on the Finland–Sweden and Estonia–Sweden routes.
The Estonia–Finland segment generated EUR 314.5 million of revenue and remained the Group’s most profitable route, although its result fell by EUR 10.9 million to EUR 70.4 million.
The Finland–Sweden result declined to EUR 1.3 million, partly reflecting 68 days of vessel maintenance, while Estonia–Sweden remained loss-making with a segment loss of EUR 1.2 million.

verified_key_information_units.information: Net debt decreased to EUR 432.4 million (from EUR 537.7 million in 2024) with a net debt/EBITDA ratio of 3.3 (vs 3.1 in 2024); cash position impacted by EUR 44.6 million dividends paid (plus EUR 11.3 million related income tax) and EUR 113.5 million in loan repayments and interest during the year.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Management Report: 'Liquidity and Cash Flow' section detailing net debt, dividend payments, and financing activities.

candidate_sentences.text: Debt reduction continued, with interest-bearing liabilities falling 19.9% to EUR 445.9 million and net debt declining to EUR 432.4 million.
However, net debt to EBITDA increased to 3.3 because EBITDA declined.
The Group paid a EUR 0.06-per-share dividend totalling EUR 44.6 million and plans to propose the same dividend for 2026.

verified_key_information_units.information: Capital investments totaled EUR 33.0 million (focused on vessel maintenance and IT systems), with planned maintenance and repair works amounting to 73 vessel-days.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Management Report: 'Liquidity and Cash Flow' and 'Investments and Vessels' sections specifying capital expenditures and maintenance days.

verified_key_information_units.information: Strategic focus on emissions reduction includes preparations to transition shuttle vessels (MyStar and Megastar) to liquified biomethane from 2026, targeting a 75% reduction in greenhouse gas emissions and cost mitigation amid regulatory pressures.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: CEO Letter to Shareholders and Sustainability Strategy and Governance section outlining biofuel transition plans and environmental targets.

verified_key_information_units.information: Post-reporting-period management changes: Paavo Nõgene resigned as Chairman of the Management Board effective May 2026; Peep Jalakas appointed as new Chairman effective April 2026; Margus Schults removed from Management Board effective February 2026 (remaining as Managing Director of Tallink Silja Oy).
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Note 25: 'Subsequent Events' and Management Report 'Events After the Reporting Period' detailing management board resignations and elections.
